title: burn-rate-alert-filtering-and-derivative-tuning-draft
content:
Summary / motivation:

This is a working note to consolidate hypotheses and proposed changes for reducing pager noise caused by burn-rate alerts and derivative-ish SLO alarms (sudden short lived spikes that do not represent customer pain). Reproducible symptoms we keep seeing: high volume of pages for 5–10 minute burn spikes followed by automatic recoveries, many alerts with identical fingerprints across hosts, and missing metrics occasionally causing false-positive burn calculations. Goal: reduce noisy pages by 60% without increasing time-to-detect genuine degradation beyond our target (5m).

Background / recent incidents: 
- Multiple on-call shifts in Jan 2024 saw noisy burn alerts for hosted-api (model-inference) routes; pages spiked 3x normal for ~6 minutes on 2024-01-11 (see SRE-472).
- Investigation found: short-lived backend throttling at ingress LB + one downstream controller emitting a burst of 500 errors for 2–3 mins; however, client-facing error rate stayed <0.5% overall.
- Pager noise contributors identified: too-sensitive derivative thresholds, alerts firing on partial telemetry (agent TTLs missing), and per-instance alerts without dedup.

Observed signals (metrics of interest):
- slo/response_success_rate{route=~"/v[12]/.*"} (windowed 5m and 1h)
- infra/request_error_rate (per-region)
- inference/latency_p95_ms (route-level)
- cache/kv_cache_hit_ratio (prefix-based)
- telemetry/metric_submission_age_seconds (to detect missing metrics)
- pager/alert_volume_by_signature (aggregate to track noise)

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
1) Aggregated derivative over short windows: current burn-rate is calculated as a derivative over a 1m window, which amplifies short transient bursts.
2) Metric gaps: agent-side metric drops (agent restarts or exporter timeouts) cause sudden apparent changes in denominators for success rate.
3) Alert duplication: per-instance rule fires independently and each instance pages on-call due to lack of grouping.
4) Misrouted client retries: retries from clients create short burst of 429/5xx that self-resolve.

Immediate mitigations (engineering + SRE):
- Short-term: add client-side debounce in alerting pipeline: require burn-rate elevated for 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets OR a 5-minute rolling-average burn > threshold.
- Add telemetry-health precondition: do not evaluate burn alerts if telemetry/metric_submission_age_seconds > 45s for the relevant exporter.
- Change paging policy: group alerts by route+signature; only page first occurrence from a given group within a 10-minute window (configurable).

Proposed alert definition changes (examples):
- Old: burn_rate = derivative(slo/response_success_rate[1m]) > 0.02 -> page
- New: burn_rate_short = derivative(slo/response_success_rate[1m])
  AND burn_rate_short > 0.02
  AND increase(slo/response_success_rate[3m]) > 0.015
  OR avg_over_time(slo/response_success_rate[5m]) < (slo_target - 0.01)
  AND telemetry/metric_submission_age_seconds < 45

Rationale: require either a sustained drop (5m average) or corroborating increase in a wider window. Add telemetry health to avoid false alarms when exporters are flakey.

Runbook (on-call steps when burn alert pages):
1) Acknowledge and immediately check telemetry/metric_submission_age_seconds for affected exporter(s). If >45s, treat as telemetry failure; escalate to infra-exporter team and suppress the burn alert for 15m (manual suppress + note).
2) Check "pager/alert_volume_by_signature" dashboard to confirm if this is a unique signature or a flood. If flood, mute duplicates and investigate common upstream (LB/edge) or client retry patterns.
3) Verify real user impact: query traces/sampled logs for affected routes in last 10m for increased 5xx or user-facing errors.
4) If user-facing impact is confirmed, run mitigation: route traffic to fallback model-variant OR scale up dedicated workers (automation: autoscale policy id: dedicated-autoscaler-3).
5) If no user-facing impact and telemetry healthy, escalate to platform infra for network/timeout spike.

Debugging queries (examples to paste in Grafana / Prometheus):
- rate(backend_errors_total{route=~"/v[12]/.*"}[1m]) by (route, instance)
- sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) by (route)
- avg_over_time(slo/response_success_rate{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])
- max(telemetry/metric_submission_age_seconds[1m]) by (exporter)

Dedup / grouping strategy (policy draft):
- Primary grouping key: {team, product_route_prefix, error_signature_hash}
- Secondary: region, cluster
- Pager-suppression window: default 10m for duplicate signature; escalates if distinct signature occurs within suppression window.

Longer-term changes / experiments (backlog):
- Implement derivative smoothing: use EWMA on the derivative to dampen single-point spikes. Experiment: alpha=0.3 over 3 windows.
- Introduce SLO burn-rate tiers: page on medium-burn only when accompanied by latency_p95_persist > threshold.
- Instrument service-level traces to flag retriable client-originated traffic vs service failures (add request header inference).
- Add synthetic checks and canary traffic to detect exporter/metric loss early.

Hypothesis testing plan (short list):
1) A/B deploy new burn alert rule for 10% of production routes for 2 weeks; compare pages/true-positives ratio. Owner: Marco. Jira: SRE-490.
2) Enable metric_health precondition on staging exporters for 1 week and simulate exporter restarts to ensure suppression behaves as expected. Owner: Priya.

Open questions / tradeoffs: 
- Suppressing pages by grouping reduces noise but increases mean time to awareness for novel failures in the same group. How to compensate? (idea: lower-signal broadcast slack channel for group events).
- What is acceptable extra detection latency? current SLA target is 5m; desired noise reduction suggests we may increase detection to ~6–7m for borderline cases.
- How to validate that missing metrics are not masking true degradations? We need a synthetic probe that exercises the full stack and reports independently.

Action items (owners + dates):
- Add metric_submission_age_seconds precondition to burn alerts (Ava) — due 2024-02-09.
- Implement grouping + suppression logic in PagerDuty connector (SRE infra) (Daniel) — due 2024-02-16.
- Create A/B experiment for new alerting rule (Marco) — create experiment plan by 2024-02-05.
- Add synthetic canary for hosted-api (product road) (product + infra) — backlog, target Q2.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally loose; looking for feedback on thresholds, grouping keys, and whether 10-minute suppression is too aggressive for our multi-tenant hosted environment. Please add comments in the linked Jira SRE-472 or reply in the Slack thread.

Attachments / logs referenced:
- SRE-472 incident timeline (Jira)
- observability PR #231 (alert-rule changes, WIP)
- Slack: #sre-ops thread 2024-01-11 for first responder notes

End of draft.
